stages.title: Characterize the existing Go API and React contract
targets: server/handlers.go and server/main.go as the unchanged system under test
server/*_test.go characterization coverage
tests/contract/ reusable black-box HTTP fixtures and assertions
client/src API call sites, payloads, Auth0 flow, and same-origin/local configuration
legacy route/configuration inventory and sanitized caller-evidence record
tests: Run the current Go test suite before adding tests and retain its result as baseline evidence.

Exercise GET/POST /api/feelings and GET/POST /api/weekly-tracker against the Go service for successful, empty, invalid, missing-token, expired-token, mismatched-user, and cross-user cases using synthetic users and non-private fixtures.

Capture status, headers, JSON shape, field representation, ordering, upsert behavior, and write side effects in reusable black-box assertions; label approved normalization differences separately from behavior that must remain compatible.
Exercise allowed/disallowed CORS preflight and retired or unmatched routes, including /api/ping, without asserting accidental quirks as target requirements.

Trace every React request and Auth0 token/header dependency to the characterized contract and record sanitized evidence that the former OpenClaw/chat/agent routes have no repository caller or active production caller.
definition_of_done: The existing Go implementation has not been behaviorally changed.
A deterministic characterization suite can run against a configurable base URL and distinguishes preserved behavior from approved normalization.
The four supported routes and all React request shapes are covered, including two-user isolation scenarios.
Route retirement evidence is recorded without tokens, subjects, notes, or other private values; contrary evidence stops retirement and returns the work to Define.
Baseline test commands and results are ready to be recorded as implementation evidence.

stages.title: Establish the pinned standalone Deno foundation
targets: api/ standalone Deno TypeScript service skeleton
deno.json and deno.lock
OCI container definition and reproducible build inputs
Deno dependency and permission compatibility record
tests: Pin a stable Deno 2 container/runtime version, run deno check and the selected test runner, and verify lockfile integrity in a clean build.
Spike the selected HTTP, strict-schema, Auth0/JWKS, PostgreSQL, logging, and test dependencies under Deno without implementing business routes.
Build and start the OCI image with only documented filesystem, network, and environment permissions; verify an unprivileged health endpoint and graceful shutdown.
Verify production dependencies do not require unsafe lifecycle scripts, unsupported native addons, or materially broader permissions than the approved design.
definition_of_done: Concrete Deno-compatible libraries and build commands are documented and locked.
The service starts reproducibly in an OCI container and emits sanitized structured startup/health logs.
No feelings, weekly, Data API, Edge Function, Storage, job, or operator behavior has been introduced.
Any failed compatibility spike returns the runtime or dependency choice to Design rather than adding a hidden workaround.

stages.title: Provision an authorized non-production Supabase target
targets: Supabase non-production project in Sydney ap-southeast-2
supabase/ local configuration and versioned migration workspace
managed secret references for migration-owner and runtime database connections
non-production backup, restore, audit, and Data API exposure settings record
tests: Before creating cloud infrastructure, record the separate explicit human authorization required by AGENTS.md; plan approval alone is insufficient.
Verify the project reports Sydney ap-southeast-2 and confirm the chosen plan's managed backup data remains in Australia before loading any representative data.
Verify direct TLS connectivity for migrations and the candidate pooled/runtime connection mode from the intended test environment without printing credentials.
Verify the application schema is absent from the Data API exposed-schema list and that no browser or service-role secret is introduced.
Run the current Supabase CLI help/version discovery and scan the current Supabase changelog for relevant breaking changes before locking provisioning commands.
definition_of_done: A separately authorized, empty, non-production Sydney project is available and identified only by non-secret configuration references.
Managed backup residency/defaults, restore access, provider audit controls, and operator access are documented without secret values.
Direct and runtime connection choices are verified against the selected container network; prepared statements are disabled if transaction pooling is retained.
No production infrastructure, data, environment, endpoint, or traffic has changed.

stages.title: Create the private Postgres schema, roles, constraints, and RLS
targets: supabase/migrations/ private feelings and weekly-tracker schema history
least-privilege migration-owner and runtime roles/grants
forced RLS policies using transaction-local app.auth0_sub
database constraint, index, and policy tests
tests: Apply all migrations to an empty local/test database, inspect migration history, roll back where defined, and reapply from zero.
Assert feelings types, defaults, status constraint, legacy ID uniqueness, and composite (user_id, created_at desc, id desc) index.
Assert weekly mood/version constraints, UNIQUE(user_id, week_of), timestamp behavior, and atomic INSERT ON CONFLICT update behavior.

With two synthetic Auth0 subjects, test SELECT/INSERT and weekly UPDATE USING/WITH CHECK policies, missing transaction identity, ownership reassignment, DELETE denial, and absence of BYPASSRLS/table ownership for the runtime role.

Verify the private schema is not Data API exposed, anon/authenticated/service-role grants are not used by the application, RLS is forced, and Supabase database/security advisors report no unresolved finding relevant to the schema.
definition_of_done: The schema matches DATA-001 through DATA-005 and can be reproduced solely from version-controlled migrations.
Database tests prove durable constraints and two-subject row isolation independently of application filters.
The runtime role has only required table operations and no DELETE, owner, BYPASSRLS, or service-role capability.
No production database migration has been applied.

stages.title: Build and validate the idempotent data migration path
targets: tools/migrate/ standalone Deno TypeScript Mongo-to-Postgres migration CLI
synthetic and representative non-production MongoDB export fixtures
sanitized reconciliation and exception-manifest formats
target-to-Mongo rollback reconciliation tool and fixtures
tests: Dry-run valid, malformed, duplicate, orphaned, mixed-type, and repeat-input fixtures without writing private content to output.
Import representative non-production feelings and weekly trackers, preserving Auth0 sub and approved timestamps while mapping source _id to legacy_mongo_id.
Run the import twice and assert stable counts, stable non-content hashes, no duplicate target rows, and explicit reporting of every rejected or conflicting source record.
Run forward reconciliation by collection and user and exercise target-to-Mongo reconciliation on synthetic target-only writes.
Require Vinicius Delascio's explicit recorded decision for each real cleanup, transformation, quarantine, or exclusion before treating reconciliation as successful.
definition_of_done: Every representative source record is deterministically migrated or appears in a sanitized exception manifest.
Repeatability and rollback reconciliation tests pass without duplicate or lost records.
Australian project and managed-backup residency evidence accompanies the dry-run report.
The migration role and Mongo dependency exist only in the CLI and are unavailable to the request-serving service.
No production data has been read, changed, or migrated without separate authorization.

stages.title: Implement the shared Auth0, authorization, and HTTP boundary
targets: api/ Auth0 access-token verification middleware
api/ transaction-local database identity and least-privilege connection wrapper
api/ strict request schemas, structured errors, CORS, logging, health, and readiness
server-only environment-variable contract without values
tests: Validate signed RS256 tokens for exact issuer, audience, expiry, and non-empty sub using a controlled JWKS test server; deny missing, malformed, expired, wrong-issuer, and wrong-audience credentials.
Verify x-user-id is optional but conflicting values return 403 and body identity cannot override the verified sub.

Prove each database operation starts an explicit short transaction, sets parameterized transaction-local app.auth0_sub, applies an explicit user_id predicate, and cannot leak identity through the connection pool.
Run two-subject application and direct-database denial tests, including ownership reassignment and DELETE attempts.

Verify allowed local CORS behavior, disallowed-origin rejection before handlers, sanitized structured errors/logs, readiness dependency checks, and absence of tokens, raw subjects, bodies, comments, notes, or secrets in captured output.
definition_of_done: The shared boundary passes security tests before any business route is enabled.
Auth0 accounts, token type, issuer/audience contract, and canonical sub remain unchanged.
The Deno service contains no service-role key, operator API, impersonation path, or browser database credential.
Required environment variable names, purpose, ownership, and secret classification are documented without values.

accepted_complexity.item: Keep the Go/Heroku/Mongo implementation and its credentials, checkpoint, and rollback tooling alongside the Deno/Supabase replacement through Review, Release, cutover, and observation.
accepted_complexity.rationale: Incremental migration and evidence-based rollback require a working source implementation until the replacement is proven; temporary duplication is safer than early decommissioning.

accepted_complexity.item: Use a custom least-privilege Postgres runtime role with forced RLS and transaction-local app.auth0_sub in addition to explicit application user filters.
accepted_complexity.rationale: Auth0 remains canonical while direct Supabase Auth/Data API integration is out of scope; the dual enforcement prevents a missing application predicate from exposing sensitive rows.

accepted_complexity.item: Maintain both forward Mongo-to-Postgres migration and post-write target-to-Mongo rollback reconciliation during migration.
accepted_complexity.rationale: A compute-only rollback after Supabase accepts writes would lose acknowledged data; the second direction is required for the approved rollback contract.

accepted_complexity.item: Add reusable black-box differential tests that run against both the Go and Deno services.
accepted_complexity.rationale: Existing tests cover only CORS and cannot prove externally observable compatibility, approved normalization, or slice-by-slice equivalence.

accepted_complexity.item: Pin Deno 2, dependencies, container inputs, and least-privilege runtime permissions while allowing vetted npm compatibility only when native web or JSR options are unsuitable.
accepted_complexity.rationale: The selected runtime is viable but adds compatibility and supply-chain verification work; explicit pinning and an early spike keep that risk bounded and reproducible.

accepted_complexity.item: Keep complete unpaginated feelings history during this migration and measure production size before release.
accepted_complexity.rationale: Pagination would change the public contract and is not approved; measured unsafe size triggers a return to Define rather than concealed scope growth.

approval.reason: Vinicius Delascio approved the execution plan, including the staged Deno/Supabase vertical slices and accepted migration complexity. This approval permits progression to implementation but does not authorize any production infrastructure, data, environment, deployment, traffic, irreversible migration, or deletion action; those remain separately gated.
